The Daily Chronicle of Musk's Companies
"Message received..." - Elon Musk (@elonmusk)
 
■ TERAFAB:
Per Elon, "Well, it’s going to be some pretty significant capital. It’s certainly in the tens of billions for Terafab. Although we’ve got to figure out what the relative split is between SpaceX and Tesla in terms of who pays for what at Terafab. But it’s not going to be less than tens of billions in capital equipment up through early 2028, and then it’ll be a lot more. It’ll probably be north of $100 billion long term."
 
- The Grimes County appraisal district now shows Terafab's WIT TECH LLC has acquired 573.82 more acers. It is now owner of 47 parcels, up from 40, covering 8,997 legal acres. There are five O'Connor tracts and two Frazier tracts. Together they carry $8,473,250 in land value and $900,820 in improvements. The two Lloyd Perry parcels totaling 101.69 acres are still pending.
 
■ SPACEX $SPCX ($144.75, -9.14%):
- A new FAA/CADENA Space Operations air-traffic planning slide lists Starship Flight 15 for a November 8th launch, and Starship Starlink 30-1 on December 10th. Interesting enough, it also lists Blue Origin New Glenn 4.1 on December 28th. Of note, these are unofficial planning targets, not confirmed launch windows.
- Per SpaceX's Q3 2026 10-Q, "As announced on our earnings call on October 20, 2026, our board of directors has formed a special committee to evaluate a potential combination between SpaceX and Tesla, Inc. (“Tesla”). The board of directors of Tesla has also formed a special committee. No determination by our special committee has been made regarding any potential combination, and any potential combination would be subject to further approval by our special committee, our board of directors and our controlling shareholder. There can be no assurance that any agreement will be reached or that any transaction will be consummated, and the special committee may determine not to proceed with recommending any transaction it does not believe to be in the best interests of our shareholders."
 
- Starship 43 rolled from Production to Massey’s for its cryo-testing campaign. Ship 43 and Booster 23 should pair for Flight 16, which could be the first Starship launch from Kennedy Space Center’s LC-39A in Florida.
- A 10,000 ft Temporary Flight Restriction for high energy testing at the Starbase launch complex will start tomorrow, October 23rd. I expect to see Super Heavy Booster 22 roll soon.
 
 
- The University of Louisiana Board today approved a lease that brings SpaceX to the Peter M. John and David M. John Wildlife and Coastal Preservation Center in Vermilion Parish; the old Pecan Island school. UL Lafayette (@ULLafayetteSystem) will lease the school building and about 5 acres to Ragin’ Cajun Facilities, Inc., a UL-affiliated nonprofit, for $1 per year for 40 years. That nonprofit will sublease the property to SpaceX for the same term, with property improvements in lieu of cash rent. Exhibit A listing those improvements was blank in the board materials. Allowed uses include housing, warehousing, and fabrication. At the meeting, officials noted SpaceX wants immediate access ahead of a possible sale as soon as next year. The facility includes offices, an Olympic-sized pool, basketball court, tennis court, and track.
 
- The Air Force Research Laboratory (AFRL, @AFResearchLab) tested Rocket Cargo point-to-point delivery on the October 20th Bandwagon-5 launch via SpaceX’s Starfall reentry capsule. AFRL agile cargo pods inside the capsule carried a SATCOM-enabled tracker, batteries, a reverse osmosis desalinator, survival gear, and emergency medical equipment, with sensors measuring temperature, shock, and vibration during launch and reentry. Engineers also fit-checked a UNI-PAC III life raft for possible future use. The test evaluates whether commercial rockets can rapidly deliver critical supplies worldwide to sites without roads or runways, supporting future military resupply, rescue operations, and disaster relief. 
Per Brig. Gen. Douglas P. Wickert, AFRL commander and Department of the Air Force Technology Executive Officer, "Today’s launch was another demonstration of how AFRL is partnering with industry to burn down risk, collect hard data and deliver war-winning technologies for the operational force."
Per Adam Remaly, Director of AFRL Technology Transition Office, "This was a critical achievement to demonstrate the potential of Rocket Cargo delivery for point-to-point rapid global mobility for the Future Force."
 
- SpaceX VP of Launch Kiko Dontchev (@TurkeyBeaver), Sr. Director of Starship Launch Justin Styer (@jstyer), and Principal Launch Engineer Mark Soltys joined a sold-out screening of the Starship docuseries at the Historic Cocoa Village Playhouse in Cocoa Village, Florida. They shared stories from their SpaceX careers, work on the human spaceflight program, and upcoming Starship operations on Florida’s Space Coast. All ticket proceeds supported the Restore Our Shores program for the Indian River Lagoon. Pics by Max Evans (@_MaxQ_).
 
- Expect an update about Artemis III and IV and Starship tomorrow.
COUNTDOWN TO 145 (116 - Falcon 9, 3 - Falcon Heavy, and 3 - Starship):
Launch 123! Thursday, 22nd of October, at 3:51 p.m. PT, Falcon 9 Starlink 15-15 will launch from Space Launch Complex 4E (SLC-4E) at Vandenberg Space Force Base, California. Booster B1063 will land on drone ship Of Course I Still Love You in the Pacific Ocean.
Launch 124! Sunday, 25th of October, at 10:00 p.m. PT, Falcon 9 Starlink 15-16 will launch from Space Launch Complex 4E (SLC-4E) at Vandenberg Space Force Base, California. Booster B1082 will land on drone ship Of Course I Still Love You in the Pacific Ocean.
Launch 125! Wednesday, 28th of October, at 9:17 p.m. PT, Falcon 9 Starlink 15-18 will launch from Space Launch Complex 4E (SLC-4E) at Vandenberg Space Force Base, California. Booster B1093 will land on drone ship Of Course I Still Love You in the Pacific Ocean.
Launch 126! Wednesday, 4th of November, at 9:14 p.m. PT, Falcon 9 Starlink 15-21 will launch from Space Launch Complex 4E (SLC-4E) at Vandenberg Space Force Base, California. The booster will land on drone ship Of Course I Still Love You in the Pacific Ocean.
Launch 127! Thursday, 5th of November, at 2:34 p.m. PT, Falcon 9 NROL-195 will launch from Space Launch Complex 4E (SLC-4E) at Vandenberg Space Force Base, California. The booster will Return to Launch Site (RTLS) at Vandenberg and land at Landing Zone 4 (LZ-4). This the 15th batch of satellites for a reconnaissance satellite constellation built by SpaceX and Northrop Grumman for the National Reconnaissance Office to provide imaging and other reconnaissance capabilities. NRO missions support national security by providing critical intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance capabilities from space.
 
■ TESLA $TSLA ($374.58, -3.08%):
 
- Today Fort Bend County commissioners approved four agreements today for Tesla’s proposed ~$10.1 billion vertically integrated solar cell and module manufacturing plant, Project Crystal Sun. The agreements included:
Property Tax Abatement Agreement between Fort Bend County and Tesla located in Precinct 2, Reinvestment Zone No. 34. in a Precinct 2 reinvestment zone.
Chapter 381 Economic Development Agreement between Fort Bend County, Texas and Tesla to encourage investment and job creation in Fort Bend County.
Foreign Trade Zone Site Non-Objection and Payment in Lieu of Certain Taxes Agreement between Fort Bend County, Fort Bend County Drainage District, and Tesla, and authorize the County Judge to execute the Non-Objection. Fort Bend County payments under this Agreement would be deposited into the County General Fund and Fort Bend County Drainage payments would be deposited into the Drainage District Operating Account.
True Up Payment in Lieu of Taxes (PILOT) Agreement between Fort Bend County and Tesla with all payments under this Agreement to be deposited into the County General Fund.
Combined with the earlier August reinvestment zone and the September unanimous Lamar CISD approval of the 10-year JETI school property tax limitation, the major local steps are complete.
 
- There are reports that Samsung Electro-Mechanics will receive about 3.7 trillion won (~$2.8 billion) from Tesla and NVIDIA to expand FC-BGA (flip-chip ball grid array) substrate production for AI semiconductors. Tesla is reported to contribute ~1.1 trillion won and NVIDIA ~2.6 trillion won toward dedicated lines primarily in Sejong, South Korea. The substrates would support AI chips for Tesla’s autonomous vehicles and Optimus robots under a five-year supply agreement from 2029 through 2033, with mass production targeted for the second half of 2028. NVIDIA has also publicly discussed substrate capacity partnerships with the company.
- Per Tesla's Q3 2026 10-Q, "The Tesla board of directors has formed a special committee (the “Special Committee”) comprising disinterested directors to explore deepening Tesla’s relationship with SpaceX, which could be through certain arrangements including without limitation a business combination (a “Transaction”). While there could be merits to a Transaction, there is no assurance that any such Transaction will be consummated, as a Transaction would be subject to, among other things, the affirmative recommendation of the Special Committee and, if agreed upon, any necessary shareholder approval."
 
- The Tesla Lithium Refinery was recognized as a 2026 Coastal Bend Bays Foundation Environmental Award Industry recipient for Sustainable Innovation and Community Engagement. It was presented at the Environmental Awards Celebration and 35th Anniversary event in Corpus Christi. Jason Bevan, Plant Manager, accepted the Industry award on behalf of the refinery. Pic by Klarissa Garcia, Tesla Lithium Refinery Community & Site Relations.
Per Tesla VP of Vehicle Engineering, Lars Moravy (@larsmoravy), on the Roadster Rocket variant, "We don’t show things that we can’t do in production. The cold gas system can produce over 80kN of force. If everything weighs even a ridiculously high 2500 kg with the mass of gas plus the thruster system, the lift from the thrusters is >3x the mass of the vehicle. When you have more lift than mass, you can get off the ground, when it’s that much more over time you have spare air to flip and maneuver... Simple math really…."
 
- Storm has installed the 106 Tesla Megapack 2XLs at its Langerlo battery park in Genk-Zuid, Belgium, on the site of the former Langerlo coal-fired power plant. The park is planned for 100 MW of power and 400 MWh of storage and is scheduled to become operational in 2027. Flemish Minister Jo Brouns and Mayor Wim Dries visited the site today.
- Tesla recognized $221 million of revenue and $171 million of cost of revenues from SpaceX Megapack purchases in Q3, bringing the nine-month total to $626 million of revenue and $478 million of cost of revenues. As of September 30th, accounts receivable from SpaceX stood at $729 million and deferred revenue on those contracts was $648 million. Of those amounts, $588 million related to Megapacks not yet delivered. Net of undelivered units, accounts receivable was $141 million and deferred revenue was $60 million.
- Texas DMV records show 449 Cybercabs and 362 Model Y Robotaxis authorized to drive without a safety driver.
 
■ THE BORING COMPANY:
 
 
- Michel (@Mic_VegasSphere) hit the Vegas Monorail and checked out the Vegas LOOP airport tunnel at the Westgate station. It looks complete and ready, with no construction activity visible. The ~2-mile twin tunnels run under Paradise Road to the Boring Company's owned site at 4744 Paradise.  Both tunnels will open together. The stretch is expected to bring three new stations online: 4744 Paradise, Virgin Hotels Las Vegas, and the former Gordon Biersch site.
 
- Michel also reported that the enlarged underground Central Hall station at the Las Vegas Convention Center now has a new downward ramp with concrete walls. Parking has been restored over the covered pit. The ramp connects above ground to the Encore tunnel ring and is positioned to link Central toward the airport tunnel interchange. This allows vehicles to stay in the system when traveling between Riviera/Fontainebleau and Encore, and it ties Central into the airport direction. Loop service is running elsewhere, but Convention Center stations remain unavailable while the underground Central work finishes.
 
- TBC VP of Business Development, Jim Fitzgerald (@FJ_Fitzgerald), hosted former Texas Land Commissione, George P. Bush, and Mark Havens, both of Pine Cove Strategies, at the Bastrop HQ. Pine Cove Strategies is an Austin-based government relations and strategic consulting firm. "The visit offered a fascinating firsthand look at the company's innovative approach to addressing complex transportation, infrastructure, and logistics challenges. Texas continues to attract companies pushing the boundaries of what's possible, creating new opportunities for economic development and reinforcing the state's reputation as a hub for innovation and entrepreneurship."
 
■ NEURALINK:
 
- Neuralink Head of Medical Affairs, Dr. David McMullen (@DavidMcMullen), spoke at Jersey Shore University Medical Center’s Neurosurgery for the Visiting Professor Grand Rounds. He was with Shabbar Danish, Chairman of the University Medical Center. David discussed the rapidly evolving field of brain-computer interfaces and Neuralink’s work in the area. He joined Neuralink in December 2025 after serving as director of the FDA’s Office of Neurological and Physical Medicine Devices. He previously worked at the NIH and DARPA and contributed to early human BCI systems. The hospital event focused on how neurosurgeons can stay current with BCI technology for patient care.
- Neuralink filed a Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation project TABS2027004080 that covers work for a staircase at the Del Valle Campus. Not very exciting, but the filing does give a little bit of insight into the facility. The staircase will connect a second-floor "implant space" and a third-floor "robot space."
 
■ STARLINK:
Per Elon, "Veterans of the cellular industry look at the chess board of existing pieces and don’t see a solution. They don’t understand that SpaceX is developing entirely new pieces that fundamentally alter the strategic landscape."
 
- The FCC Wireless Telecommunications Bureau granted consent for SpaceX’s Starlink Spectrum Holdings to acquire three unpaired AWS-3 licenses (1695–1710 MHz) from Tristar License Group / TLG Unpaired Holdings. The licenses cover 62 counties across eight states at ~4% of the U.S. population. Tristar never built them out. The FCC waived terrestrial construction and renewal requirements so SpaceX can use the spectrum for Starlink Mobile instead of cell towers, subject to phased uplink performance benchmarks. SpaceX’s AWS-3 holdings now attributes 75 MHz in the areas.
 
- Giovanni Gallo, SpaceX Sr. Sales Manager for LATAM, showing off the Starlink booth at Fujioka Distribuidor, a major technology and electronics wholesaler in Goiânia, Goiás, Brazil. He credited Stella Leone and Igor Coelho for the work and thanked Eduardo Miki Watanabe for the partnership. Fujioka Distribuidor is an official Starlink reseller and sells kits including the Mini and standard models through its stores, site, and televendas.
 
- Paul Spicer, a Network Delivery Engineer at Burberry, getting free Starlink Wi-Fi with 300 Mbps download speeds throughout a Virgin Atlantic flight to Los Angeles. Virgin Atlantic has completed Starlink installation on its full Airbus A350-1000 fleet and is rolling it out to 787s and A330neos, with full fleet coverage targeted by the end of 2027. The service is free for Flying Club members and membership is free to join.
 
■ 𝕏:
 
- X Japan for Small Medium Business (@BizJP) is exhibiting at ad:tech tokyo 2026 in booth C-8 at Tokyo Midtown & The Ritz-Carlton today and tomorrow. X staff are on site to explain the updated X advertising products in person for businesses interested in starting or optimizing campaigns.
- X is working on an update that lets users select more than one reply audience option at once instead of picking a single setting. Current official choices remain single-select: Everyone, Accounts you follow, Only accounts you mention, or Only verified accounts. The in-development version uses checkboxes so combinations are possible. For example, Accounts you follow + Verified accounts. After applying a multi-select restriction, the post indicates "Only some accounts can reply."
 
- Adapter (@adapter) announced it is a Launch Partner in the SpacexSI Partner Network. It is now available for Grok Bot and Grok Build and structures a user’s data and tribal knowledge into a queryable system so that each Bot or Build starts with that context already loaded. This reduces the need for searching or re-explaining context at the start of a task.
 
■ SPACEXSI:
 
- SpaceXSI launched the SpaceX Super Intelligence Partner Network, its official program for companies building products, solutions, and services with Grok. The network has two partner types:
Transformation Partners: They help customers deploy the Grok platform across the enterprise and create business value (including through a Forward Deployed Engineer accreditation program).
Marketplace Partners: They build plugins and integrations that connect Grok products to tools customers already use.
More than 130 companies joined the early-access phase. Partners receive training, tools, and support for joint customer engagements. Named participants include NVIDIA, Snowflake, Databricks, Bain & Company, Booz Allen Hamilton, Apollo Global Management, and Galatiq.
- Tech Mahindra (@tech_mahindra) announced a collaboration with SpaceXSI to use Grok Build for AI-powered software engineering and application modernization. The partnership combines Tech Mahindra’s enterprise transformation and AI consulting capabilities with SpaceXSI’s AI-powered development platform. It targets modernizing legacy applications, improving code quality, shortening development cycles, and scaling AI-assisted engineering across sectors including technology, telecommunications, banking, financial services, manufacturing, healthcare, and retail. This is the first collaboration between a major Indian IT services firm and SpaceX’s AI division.
 
- NVIDIA announced the OpenShell Reference Architecture at GTC Berlin today. SpaceXSI stated it is participating for AI agent security. Jensen Huang introduced it as a way for businesses to set boundaries for AI agents and stop them when they step outside those limits. The architecture combines NVIDIA Vera Rubin systems for models, Vera CPUs running the open-source OpenShell runtime, and BlueField-4 DPUs with NVIDIA Sentry for out-of-band monitoring and enforcement. SpaceXSI, among others,will allow enterprises to run their agents on the OpenShell infrastructure.
- Cursor's status notifications will move from status.cursor.com to status.x.ai on October 26th.
 
- Grok Bot can now use 1Password for approved logins. Users share selected vault items, approve each fill, and the Bot signs in without seeing the raw passwords. The integration is rolling out over the next few days.
 
■ ELON NEWS:
- Semafor has reported that Elon invested approximately $1 billion in Skydance, the merged Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery. The investment came around the same time as equity contributions from other investors. Skydance is led by David Ellison; son of, Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison. The company has said it aims for $6 billion in cost savings over three years while carrying substantial debt from the acquisition. Neither Elon nor Skydance has confirmed the investment and the sources were not named.
